name: Pacifism
summary: Pacifism opposes war and, in its stronger forms, all killing and violence, holding that disputes and injustices should be met by nonviolent means such as persuasion, noncooperation and civil disobedience. It ranges from absolute pacifism, which rules out violence even in self-defence, to contingent or pragmatic forms that reject war but allow some personal defence. Its roots are religious (Christian non-resistance, ahimsa) and it has liberal, anarchist and institutional variants.
scope: Mainstream principled and transformational pacifism as seen in the Tolstoyan and Garrisonian Christian non-resistance tradition, Gandhian nonviolence and the King civil rights movement, and in the philosophical typology summarised in the Stanford Encyclopedia. It excludes purely tactical nonviolence and contingent opposition to a single war. Pacifism says little about economics or social policy, so most such answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: Leo Tolstoy
keyFigures.role: Author of The Kingdom of God Is Within You, a major statement of Christian non-resistance

keyFigures.name: Mahatma Gandhi
keyFigures.role: Leader of nonviolent resistance (satyagraha) in India's independence movement

keyFigures.name: Martin Luther King Jr.
keyFigures.role: Applied Gandhian nonviolence in the US civil rights movement

sources.usedFor: Non-resistance to evil, refusal of military service and oaths, rejection of allegiance to government, and quoted Garrison and Ballou texts.

sources.title: Nonviolence
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Gandhi's ahimsa and means-ends view, noncooperation methods, King and Sharp.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a pacifist concern as such; adherents with Gandhian or Christian concern for the poor lean to support, but nothing in the sources addresses health policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inferred from the transformational strand's concern for social justice; the sources do not discuss wage law.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pacifism is silent on market efficiency and its adherents range from Tolstoyan communalists to liberal pacifists.

public-ownership.rationale: Pacifists are split between state-ownership socialists, decentralists and liberals; the sources give no common line.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from the concern for the poor in peace-church and Gandhian ethics; not stated in the sources.

unions-good.rationale: Inferred from the strikes, boycotts and non-cooperation that nonviolent theorists treat as legitimate tools of labor and civic power.

property-fundamental.rationale: Tolstoy and the non-resistants say victims should give up more property rather than resist, so property is not held as an overriding right; inferred.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from liberal and transformational pacifists' concern with structures that produce war and injustice; not directly documented.

cut-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the ethic of care for the weak; the sources do not address welfare policy.

worker-ownership.rationale: Some pacifists (Tolstoyan, anarchist-pacifist) favor cooperative property, but liberal pacifists do not; no common position.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from the civil-libertarian lean of liberal pacifism and the movement's experience of state surveillance of dissent; not documented.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The sources say nothing on drug policy; adherents split between ascetic and libertarian views.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Pacifists oppose hatred but also coercive state power; adherents are split and the sources are silent.

strong-leader.rationale: Tolstoy and Garrison deny the authority of rulers; a strong leader bypassing checks runs against the movement's distrust of concentrated coercive power.

state-harmful.rationale: Tolstoy and the Garrisonian non-resistants reject human government and Gandhi spoke of an ideal stateless order, but liberal pacifism like Holmes's works within states; the strands split.

limit-guns.rationale: Opposition to killing and to violence leads most pacifists to favor restricting weapons, though the sources do not state it for civilian guns.

empower-police-military.rationale: Pacifists seek reduced militarism and oppose funding of war; SEP notes pacifist "doves" oppose militarist budgets. Police are less clearly covered.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Nothing in the sources bears on sex work; adherents split.

decide-locally.rationale: Gandhian decentralism and Tolstoyan communalism favor local self-rule; inferred, not directly sourced here.

rehabilitation.rationale: SEP reports many pacifists reject execution and punishment by force; the aim of changing the opponent's heart in Gandhian nonviolence implies reform over retribution.

traditional-family.rationale: The sources do not address family structure; adherents range from religious conservatives (Amish, Mennonites) to progressives.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Peace churches and secular pacifists differ on this; nothing in the sources addresses it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Reverence for life pulls some pacifists to oppose abortion while others favor choice; genuinely split and not covered in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Tolstoy and the Garrisonians want a faith lived by conscience and separate from state power, so state-backed religion is disfavoured; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: King's Gandhian civil rights movement made correcting racial injustice its central aim, so adherents in that tradition support it.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the pacifist sources; adherents are split.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Garrison's declaration says "our country is the world" and rejects patriotic appeals; cultural preservation as such is not addressed, so inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: Gandhi and King pursued fast structural change by nonviolent pressure, while Quakers and liberal pacifists often work gradually; split.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from universal brotherhood ("all mankind") and the movement's welcome to conscientious objectors and refugees.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Institutional pacifism seeks international institutions to abolish war, per the Wikipedia article, but the Tolstoyan strand distrusts all governments.

free-trade.rationale: Pacifist sources do not address trade; Gandhi favored local production while liberal pacifists argued trade promotes peace.

nation-first.rationale: Garrison's declaration, quoted by Tolstoy, says "our countrymen are all mankind" and rejects patriotism as grounds for revenge or war.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: SEP says maximal pacifists reject all military force even against dictators; contingent pacifists oppose particular wars, so most adherents reject military intervention.

open-borders.rationale: Universal brotherhood implies sympathy, but open borders as policy is not addressed in the sources.

limit-growth.rationale: Gandhi's simple living supports limits but pacifists do not share a stance; sources silent.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Inferred from the transformational strand's wider concern with nonviolence toward nature; not documented.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Gandhi's critique of industrial modernity and the pacifist view that war technology multiplies killing suggest scepticism; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Nuclear weapons are opposed but power is a separate question; inferred from anti-nuclear peace movement, low confidence.

revolution-justified.rationale: Pacifists accept nonviolent revolutions (SEP cites the velvet revolutions) but reject violent ones; the statement does not say which, so adherents split.

experts-over-public.rationale: Tolstoy and Gandhian ethics trust ordinary conscience over elites; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Inferred from distrust of concentrated coercive state power; sources do not address economic planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources are silent on economic form and adherents range widely.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tolstoy was a Georgist late in life, but this is not a common pacifist position and the sources do not cover it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed by the pacifist sources.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed by the pacifist sources; adherents split.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Gandhi's swadeshi favored protecting local industry but liberal pacifists favor trade; not addressed in the sources used.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from distrust of coercive state power and war economies; not directly sourced.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Tolstoy was sceptical of landowning and trade (Helchitsky), while others accept small property; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Only the Tolstoyan fringe goes this way; mainstream pacifism has no position.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the movement's preference for voluntary action over state-organized bodies; not sourced.

one-party-rule.rationale: Pacifists reject coercive state domination and one-party rule depends on force; Tolstoy and Garrison deny any government's claim to command.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The non-resistance texts deny that rulers are divinely ordained and reject allegiance to government by force.

democracy-best.rationale: Holmes's liberal pacifism ties modern warfare's conflict with liberal-democratic values; the Tolstoyan strand dissents, so medium.

direct-votes.rationale: Not addressed; participatory sympathies are present but not documented.

right-to-secede.rationale: Consistent with the Garrisonian rejection of coercion to hold a state together, but not stated.

natural-rulers.rationale: Garrison's and Tolstoy's texts reject rulers' claim to command and affirm brotherhood of all mankind.

political-violence-never.rationale: SEP defines absolute pacifism as holding that war and violence are always wrong; Tolstoy and Gandhi rule out violent means, though contingent pacifists would allow exceptions.

war-builds-character.rationale: Pacifists hold war to be gravely evil; SEP's War entry calls it among the worst things we can do and the pacifist tradition rejects it.

separate-church-state.rationale: Tolstoy criticised the Church for blessing the military oath and arms, and the Garrisonian tradition rejects state religion; the peace churches historically seek independence.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Tolstoy takes scripture as a personal law of conscience but rejects enforcing it through state coercion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The statement requires private armed defense and policing; non-resistants deny courts and force even for private disputes (Musser, Garrison).

military-superiority.rationale: Pacifism opposes the military itself; institutional pacifists call for abolishing militaries.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Garrison's declaration says "our countrymen are all mankind"; ethnic nationhood is opposed in the movement.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Pacifists reject class war as violence; the claim as historical theory is not addressed, so inferred.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed by the pacifist sources; adherents split.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Wikipedia names Te Whiti-o-Rongomai as a pacifist leader of nonviolent Maori land resistance; general policy not stated.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Gandhi led resistance to colonial rule; reparations are not mentioned in the sources, so inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from universal brotherhood against bloc politics; not addressed.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Tolstoy's Christian non-resistance and Gandhi's ahimsa rest on self-denial and love for others, not self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Pacifist traditions split between duty-based religious ethics and Holmes's rights-based liberalism.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: SEP says pacifism can extend to nonviolence toward all sentient beings, and ahimsa in Jainism covers plants and animals.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Gandhi's critique of industrial modernity and Tolstoy's agrarian leanings sit apart from liberal pacifists; split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Gandhi distrusted machine civilization, and pacifists dislike technology that scales killing; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Pacifist writings concern violence and war, not bodily technology, so adherents have no shared view and the answer is neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from the stress on personal conscience and moral responsibility; not sourced.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Inferred from civil-libertarian lean and dissenters' interest in privacy from the state.

restore-past-order.rationale: Pacifism is a transformational project aiming at a peaceful future, not restoration; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Principled pacifists hold moral rules (Gandhi's means as seed) above outcomes, though pragmatic pacifism is consequentialist; split with a lean against.

direct-action.rationale: Gandhi's noncooperation, boycotts, strikes and sit-ins are nonviolent direct action, though pacifists also use electoral routes.

means-match-ends.rationale: Gandhi compared means to a seed and ends to a tree, and King said means must be as pure as ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Gandhi's village economy was agrarian, not foraging; the idea is outside pacifist concerns.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Neither the Tolstoyan nor the Gandhian sources make the division of labor an issue, though Tolstoy praised manual work; no common stance.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not addressed by the pacifist sources; Christian and Gandhian concern for the poor leans positive but ambiguous.

production-for-use.rationale: Not addressed; Gandhian local production sympathizes but this is not an agreed pacifist position.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Pacifism has no labor theory of profit; Christian and Gandhian critics of wealth differ from liberal pacifists, so adherents are split.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The statement demands coercive dictatorial power; the non-resistant tradition refuses any rule by force.

collective-farming.rationale: Tolstoyan communities existed but the sources do not make collective farming a pacifist position.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Some pacifists blame economic interests for war but the movement has no common doctrine; not addressed in sources.

taxation-theft.rationale: Ballou's catechism says a Christian should not voluntarily pay taxes to a force-based government but not resist collection; this is closer to conscientious refusal than the libertarian claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Holmes's liberal pacifism and the pacifist focus on harm to others fit the principle, but the strict state-restriction wording is not stated.

conscription.rationale: SEP says pacifists often refuse military service, and Holmes holds that no one may command others to kill.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Pacifists stress voice and noncooperation over exit; inferred.

positive-liberty.rationale: Transformational pacifism seeks social change for material justice; inferred.

media-academia-power.rationale: This is a claim about who holds political power; pacifist sources never weigh universities against elected officials, so no position follows.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Garrison's "all mankind" universalism contradicts racial hierarchy, though the empirical claim is not discussed.

organic-representation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the distrust of corporate state forms.

total-state.rationale: Total control of all life by the state contradicts the non-resistants' refusal of government coercion and allegiance.

national-rebirth.rationale: Pacifists reject nationalist redemption movements tied to war; inferred from rejection of patriotism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pacifists oppose war between states and aggressive war; Mohists opposed aggressive war.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The oath to a lord is opposed in the non-resistants' tradition, which refuses oaths and military service.

bound-labor.rationale: Coerced labor conflicts with Garrison's abolitionist non-resistance and Tolstoy's stance against coercion.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Pacifism's sources argue ethics and politics, not the sociology of knowledge, and adherents range from religious absolutists to secular liberals.

universal-morality.rationale: Pacifists like Gandhi and Tolstoy appeal to universal moral law, but reasoned knowability is not stated.

single-common-good.rationale: Pacifists share an aim of peace but the sources do not say whether politics should seek one rationally derived good or balance interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Pacifists split on Zionism and the sources do not address it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Nothing in the pacifist sources concerns diaspora return; the answer is indifferent, though universal brotherhood might lean favorable.

revive-national-language.rationale: Language revival is a nationalist cultural project outside the pacifist sources, and adherents have no common view.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Pacifist texts do not address how firms should be governed; some Tolstoyan and cooperative sympathizers agree while liberal pacifists are indifferent.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not a pacifist topic, and adherents split between public-school defenders and religious-school supporters such as peace churches.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is outside what pacifist sources discuss, and adherents hold the full range of macroeconomic views.

economic-freedom.rationale: Liberal pacifists link liberty and peace, but Tolstoyan and Gandhian critics of markets disagree, so there is no shared answer.

rule-by-example.rationale: Tolstoy holds that moral example and love, not force, should change society; whether rulers should govern mainly by example is inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Gandhi's independence campaign sought self-rule by nonviolent means; the statement is not addressed in general.

force-without-un.rationale: Pacifists reject military force in general, so unilateral force is rejected a fortiori.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Tolstoy and Gandhi rest nonviolence on religious conviction, though pragmatic pacifists argue from consequences.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from compassion for the poor; not documented.

class-collaboration.rationale: Gandhian nonviolence seeks to win over opponents rather than defeat them, so cooperation is favored; inferred.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Futurist destruction is opposed to the nonviolent ethic of reverence for life and works; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Not addressed; anti-colonial nonviolence exists but a common front against Western powers is not a pacifist position.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Not addressed; pacifist movements included many women (Suttner, Rankin), but inference is weak.

ban-interest.rationale: Helchitsky and Tolstoy were critical of trade but sources don't address usury.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: King led nonviolent resistance to segregation law, with Gandhian nonviolence.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Tolstoy saw the state as an instrument of violence, but the class framing is not pacifist doctrine.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from the environmental and nonviolence-toward-nature lean; not sourced.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from universal brotherhood and rejection of patriotic compulsion.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory with no basis in pacifist sources; hostile to universal brotherhood.

proportional-representation.rationale: Voting systems are not discussed in the pacifist sources and adherents have no common preference.

national-mission.rationale: Spreading a form of government to others is typically via force; Garrison rejects national allegiance and Tolstoy rejects coercive missions.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Tolstoy was sharply critical of rulers, but a general claim about elites is not stated; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Coercive state control of reproduction contradicts the refusal of violence and equal worth.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from opposition to unjust killing; not stated.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A state defending the country is excluded by pacifism, and non-resistants reject courts and force as well.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Contradicts universal brotherhood in Garrison's declaration.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Garrison's declaration: "our countrymen are all mankind"; King and Gandhi built their movements on the equal dignity of opponents.

socialism-one-country.rationale: This is a Marxist debate about revolutionary strategy that pacifist sources do not engage; pacifists reject violent revolution everywhere anyway.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Pacifist sources do not address personal law; the principle of religious exemption in conscientious objection pulls one way and equal treatment the other.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Coercion in matters of conscience is rejected by the non-resistant tradition.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Gandhi favored cow protection but wanted it by persuasion; pacifists split on legal bans.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Peace-church and secular pacifists divide on religious instruction in schools, and the sources do not address it.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A strengthened socialist state against hostile states rests on military force, rejected by pacifists.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Holmes argues that no one may command others to kill, implying legitimacy needs more than command; not directly stated.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist export policy is not a pacifist topic; liberal pacifists favor open trade while Gandhians favor self-reliance, so no common line.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced expulsion is violence and conflicts with the refusal of coercion.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Pacifism holds violence always wrong, which includes initiating force, though the property clause is not itself a pacifist concern.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Tolstoy and Gandhi hold that love and cooperation, not struggle between peoples, shape a good society.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Pacifists accept moral rejection of violent movements but generally oppose repression; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Inferred from liberal pacifism's concern for freedom from arbitrary power; not sourced.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; liberal pacifists yes, Tolstoyans no.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined revolutionary vanguard conflicts with the nonviolent and conscience-led approach.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Inferred from Christian and Gandhian concern for the weak.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: A British housing-tenure policy never discussed by pacifist sources; adherents have no shared position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Strikes and boycotts are standard nonviolent noncooperation tools (Nonviolence article).

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Pacifist sources trace misery to war and injustice rather than demography, but they do not take a position on this causal claim.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Contradicts universal brotherhood and the movement's multi-ethnic outlook.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Sortition is not addressed in the pacifist tradition, so adherents have no shared view.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Coercion against internal enemies is rejected by non-resistance.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are outside the pacifist sources; concern for the poor might support them but market-friendly pacifists would not.

party-controls-media.rationale: Coercive information control conflicts with conscience and persuasion-based change.

party-commands-army.rationale: The statement presupposes armed forces; pacifists oppose them (institutional pacifism calls for abolition).

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pacifists' simple-living ethic might sympathize, but Tolstoy, Gandhi and the SEP say nothing on legislators' pay.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Binding individuals to party decisions conflicts with conscience-based refusal.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Institutional pacifism supports supranational peace institutions; the EU is not discussed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Command of armed forces is rejected by pacifists; the statement presupposes it.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; peace churches generally have congregational governance, but this is a different question.

clerical-rule.rationale: Tolstoy attacked Church complicity with state violence; coercive clerical rule contradicts non-resistance.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Pacifists oppose the war but not by taking a side; Russell's relative pacifism aside, siding against one's government is not the stance.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Inferred from the preference for persuasion over coercion.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Term limits are not a pacifist concern, and nothing in the sources bears on the question.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Institutional pacifism wants militaries abolished; ending permanent military blocs and bases fits, though collective security is not rejected by all.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Pacifist sources have no housing doctrine, and a ban on renting is not associated with any pacifist current.

people-in-arms.rationale: An armed citizenry is still armed violence and is rejected by pacifism.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Tolstoy's agrarian leanings and Gandhi's village ideal point this way; split among others.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Pacifists would want reunification pursued peacefully, but the sources do not take a view on whether divided nations should be reunified.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: This is a populist cultural claim that pacifist sources never address; adherents include many academics and many plain-spoken religious pacifists.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Universal brotherhood suggests equal respect; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: SEP says many pacifists oppose the death penalty, and maximal pacifists reject it outright.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Peace churches and secular pacifists differ on sex education and the sources do not address curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious pacifists such as Mennonites and secular peace activists divide on this, and the sources give no position.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not discussed by pacifist sources; some religious pacifists favor restriction while liberal pacifists oppose state censorship.

minority-language-support.rationale: Inferred from respect for all peoples; not addressed.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Conscientious objection is exactly an exemption from a general law (military service) for religious conviction, so adherents favor such exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Conscientious objection is nonconformity, but Mill's argument is not discussed.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Pacifist sources do not discuss sovereign debt; concern for the poor suggests sympathy but no documented position.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from liberal and religious liberty; not addressed.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Inferred from the ethic of care for the poor.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Pacifists reject nuclear weapons as the extreme form of war; Holmes holds that modern warfare runs counter to liberal values.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional design of the presidency is not a pacifist question, and no source takes a view.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking is not discussed in pacifist sources, so adherents hold no shared view.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Pacifists prefer concessions over war, so refusing land for peace is rejected.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Tolstoy and Helchitsky criticised landowning; the common-good limit is inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate about the Soviet economy within Marxism; the pacifist sources used here do not address it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the ethic of avoiding harm; not documented.

collective-defense.rationale: Collective defense commits states to war on behalf of allies and runs against institutional pacifism.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Opposition to annexation by force is consistent; the legal claim is inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Tolstoy criticizes state-church ties; subordination by the state is not endorsed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a ceremonial head of state is not discussed in pacifist sources and adherents differ.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Pacifists oppose armed coercion between governments and their regions; the Union's "police action" is noted as an exception by some, not central.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A one-country-two-systems arrangement is not addressed by pacifist sources, though peaceful accommodation would be welcomed.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The non-resistance texts reject the divine ordination of rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax-rate structure is outside the pacifist sources; progressive-minded and libertarian pacifists differ.

character-from-environment.rationale: Pacifism holds people can change through example and love; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Garrison and Tolstoy reject rulers' claim to command by force; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Pacifists oppose militarizing space but the sources do not say whether expansion should be a central civilizational goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is not engaged by the pacifist sources, and Tolstoyans reject government form altogether.

leader-cult.rationale: Tolstoy and Garrison reject allegiance to rulers.

equal-parenting.rationale: Pacifist sources never discuss custody law, so adherents have no common position.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine about party conflict that the pacifist sources do not discuss.

land-redistribution.rationale: Tolstoy opposed landownership, but pacifists reject forcible seizure, so split.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from opposition to expulsion by force.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Claims extending borders are typically pursued by force and against universal brotherhood.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Coercion in matters of conscience is rejected.

women-must-cover.rationale: Coercion by law is opposed by the non-resistant tradition.

common-currency.rationale: Monetary union is not a pacifist topic, although some pacifists support European integration for peace; no documented position.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-nationalist union is not addressed by pacifist sources, and universal brotherhood does not decide for or against regional blocs.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not addressed in the sources, so adherents have no common stance.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: King and Gandhi pursued equal rights in the places they lived.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: This is a historical-materialist claim; pacifist sources emphasize moral and religious motives but do not rule on historical causation.

ban-cartels.rationale: Antitrust policy is not discussed in pacifist sources, and no shared position exists.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailout policy is outside pacifist sources, so there is no shared view among adherents.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred from liberal pacifism's protection of conscience against majorities (e.g., objectors).

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Quotas for public bodies are not discussed by the pacifist sources; many pacifist women's groups exist but no position is documented.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Gandhian self-reliance exists, but autarkic blocs with colonies reflect imperialism.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from concern for justice and nature; not documented.

moral-incentives.rationale: Tolstoy's ethic of moral duty over material gain; low as it concerns planned economies.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: An armed vanguard is armed violence, rejected by absolute and most other pacifists.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Garrison and Tolstoy reject the claim of rulers to special authority; inferred for titles.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Gandhi's anti-colonial nonviolence rejected imperial rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Garrison rejects patriotism as grounds for war, and objectors resist military oaths.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Pacifist sources do not discuss affirmative action; King's tradition supports redress while others favor colorblind rules.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary system design is not a pacifist topic, and sources give no position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The question is a Marxist crisis debate; pacifist sources do not address whether capitalism avoids collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from opposition to imperial projects.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency-theory strategy is outside pacifist sources; Gandhian self-reliance leans yes but liberal pacifists favor integration.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist claim about workers in rich countries that pacifist sources do not consider.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: King's movement opposed private discrimination through persuasion and protest; legal ban not stated.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal pacifism protects conscience as a right; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Pacifists oppose colonial rule but the sources say nothing on the legal force of colonial-era boundary treaties.

minority-veto.rationale: Quaker consensus practice exists but is not a pacifist political doctrine.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Nonviolent resistance to unjust rulers is endorsed, but removal in the statement is silent on means.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Pacifist sources do not discuss parliamentary sovereignty, and Tolstoyans reject legislatures entirely, so no common view.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: SEP says pacifism may extend to nonviolence toward all sentient beings, and Gandhi's ahimsa included animals.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Ahimsa leads many pacifists toward vegetarianism, so use of animals for food is more disfavored; adherents vary.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: A duty of the privileged to the poor fits Christian charity, but the pacifist sources do not state it or take a class view.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Gandhi and King were active political leaders; only the Tolstoyan strand withdraws.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Despite the word, this is a Frankfurt School claim about media and conformity, not about pacifism; the sources do not address it.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Not addressed; Sharp's cooperation theory fits but not the culture claim.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A world-systems claim not discussed by the pacifist sources, so no shared view exists.

party-own-road.rationale: Not addressed by the pacifist sources; the question is about communist party strategy.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Gandhian self-reliance leans yes, but pacifists also back aid to the poor; split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Demanding territory lost in war invites new war; pacifists favor settling disputes without force.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Pacifism does not address leadership by pre-colonial peoples' descendants, though Te Whiti shows an indigenous pacifist leader; no position.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Pacifists oppose fascism's violence but are split over resisting it by war, and sources do not address constitutional wording.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Garrison's non-resistance was bound up with abolitionism, which treated slavery as the central evil; the historical claim is not addressed, so low.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Pacifist sources do not address monuments, and adherents split between remembrance and removal.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Pacifist sources do not address gendered disadvantage in health or education, so adherents are split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Pacifists oppose all violence, but the equal-treatment claim is not addressed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Pacifism's universal ethic cuts against civilizational relativism, but the sources do not discuss institutional design across civilizations.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Pacifists reject military power and its political role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Pacifist sources do not address valuing domestic labor; adherents have no common view.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil-service recruitment is not discussed in pacifist sources and there is no shared answer.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Pacifist sources do not discuss foreign ownership of strategic firms, and adherents differ.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed; peace churches and secular pacifists differ.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Binding and recalling representatives is not addressed in pacifist sources; participatory sympathies make it uncertain.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is outside the pacifist sources, so adherents hold no shared view.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Tolstoy's later Georgist leanings point here but this is not a pacifist norm.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Not addressed; war-tax objectors would welcome parliamentary control of war budgets but the sources do not say so.

single-official-language.rationale: Inferred from respect for all peoples and opposition to coercion.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: King's tradition opposed discriminatory outcomes but the sources do not address the legal test of disparate impact.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Gandhi's simple living supports this; the sources only partly cover it.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Arming insurgents funds killing, which is rejected by absolute and contingent pacifists.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Military invasion of an ally is war and aggression, rejected by pacifists.

corporate-influence.rationale: Inferred from liberal pacifism's critique of the military-industrial complex; not documented.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Inferred from the movement's civil-libertarian lean and reliance on transnational support.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population and family incentives are not addressed by pacifist sources, and there is no shared view.

job-guarantee.rationale: A state employer of last resort is not discussed by the pacifist sources, and adherents' economic views vary.

democratic-peace.rationale: SEP cites Doyle's thesis that democracies do not fight one another; Holmes ties liberal democracy to peace, though democratization by force is rejected.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Garrison's declaration and the objector tradition hold that conscience overrides state commands such as military service.

non-intervention.rationale: Pacifists oppose armed intervention but support nonviolent aid; the statement's "for any reason" is broader.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union organization form is not a pacifist question, although nonviolent theorists value strikes generally; no position.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Tolstoy's late writing was critical of marriage law but the mainstream pacifist sources do not address it, so adherents split.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Inferred from war-resistance campaigns' use of open information; not documented.

local-production.rationale: Gandhi's swadeshi stressed local production; the sources used only partly cover it.

informal-organisation.rationale: Anarchist pacifists agree while mainstream organizations are formal; split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Institutional pacifism supports international law and courts as an alternative to war.

religious-nation.rationale: Inferred from universal brotherhood and the Bahai and Christian teachings of unity.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from opposition to hierarchy and tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Fiscal federalism is outside pacifist sources and adherents have no shared view.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Tolstoyan communities limited possessions but pacifist sources do not set a rule on personal property under common ownership.

defeat-communism.rationale: The statement treats a state or ideology as to be defeated; pacifists favor coexistence and negotiation rather than war.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Public-service delivery models are outside pacifist sources, so adherents have no common view.

religion-illusion.rationale: Tolstoy and Gandhi grounded nonviolence in religious conviction, though secular pacifists exist.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Pacifist sources do not weigh in on capitalism's historical role, and Gandhian and liberal pacifists would answer differently.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Pacifist sources do not link women's equality to economic transformation, though many pacifist figures were women; no common stance.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of childcare is not discussed in the pacifist sources, so there is no shared view.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the preference for lawful, negotiated settlement over force.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Tolstoyan colonies and Gandhian ashrams were small cooperative communities; others do not share this.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement to alter demography is coercive and conflicts with universal brotherhood.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Gandhi and Tolstoy sought a third course of village or communal life, but liberal pacifists accept markets; split and not documented in the sources.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred from universalist rejection of territorial claims enforced by war.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The sources do not address the history; denial is incompatible with the pacifist moral stance and with equal worth.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Criminal penalties are coercive and opposed by most pacifists, though some religious pacifists hold conservative views.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppression requires force and violates conscience-based dissent.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Tolstoy and Garrison reject state coercion in matters of faith.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Gandhi's campaign rejected imperial exploitation of colonies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Obliging armed resistance is incompatible with pacifism, although Bahai teaching abolishes holy war.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Armed overthrow of rulers is violence, rejected by pacifists.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred; Gandhian and liberal strands favour active citizenship.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Pacifism addresses violence and injustice but its sources do not engage the intersectionality framework.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Pacifist sources do not address gender identity and adherents range from religious conservatives to progressives.

assisted-dying.rationale: Reverence for life pulls some against while autonomy pulls others for; the sources do not say.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Pacifists come from the right (religious conservatives) and left, and its sources do not judge the left-right axis.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept; Tolstoy and Gandhi praised meaningful manual work, but no pacifist source states the claim, so neutral.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Contradicts universal brotherhood and the Quaker and Gandhian respect for other faiths.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Gandhi tied political freedom to village economy but the claim is not a common pacifist position and the sources do not discuss it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed by the pacifist sources.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Institutional pacifism calls for abolishing militaries and war, though many pacifists stop short of this.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Tolstoy's non-resistance denies governments any binding authority, divine or popular; this is inferred, and religious pacifists vary.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Pacifism has no position on religious dress; adherents are split between secularists and religious communities.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred from the transformational strand's concern for justice for victims of harm; the sources do not discuss contracts.

social-market-economy.rationale: Pacifism is silent on economic order and its adherents range from communalists to liberals.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from Gandhian and Christian concern for the poor and for means matching ends; the sources do not discuss development.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Rejection of war implies refusing membership in military alliances, which prepare for war; the sources state the anti-war principle rather than bloc policy.

missingStatements.rationale: Absolute and most principled pacifists hold that war is always wrong, though contingent pacifists reject only particular wars.

missingStatements.text: Countries should abolish their armed forces.
missingStatements.rationale: Institutional pacifism calls for abolishing militaries and war, as described in the sources.

notes: Contingent and pragmatic pacifists would answer the war-related items similarly but more softly, and would accept personal self-defence. The Tolstoyan anarchist strand rejects the state outright, which mainstream Gandhian and liberal pacifists do not.
